attribution.note: Marcus's own numbered argument in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the no-moat antecedent and the 90% threshold. 'AI market' follows from context. Firm 'is not going to', so it is a scoreable conditional forecast with no deadline.

contract.note: Marcus named no market, denominator or definition of moat. The contract's reading is ordinary and fair, and it correctly says that interim shares below 90% cannot settle a forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: March 2026 preprint on falling HHI in LLM inference. It predates the post, covers a narrower market, and does not establish the antecedent.

reviews.rationale: This conditional forecast has no deadline. Its antecedent (no moat) is not established in the packet. No evidence shows any provider reaching 90% of a defined market. A conditional with an unknown antecedent is not scored, and interim fragmentation cannot confirm a forecast with no deadline.

attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own labelled 'Prediction' tweet and endorses it in the post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will be remembered' about 2026. 'On AI investments' fits the context (SpaceX, Anthropic, OpenAI listings). The caveat about unknown collapse timing is kept.

contract.note: Reading 'holding the bag' as 2026 exposure followed by material losses is ordinary and fair. Treating 2026 as the year exposure occurred, with losses possibly realised later, follows Marcus's own timing caveat.

evidence.note: October 2026 report: SpaceX fell after joining the index but by late October was only about 2% below its opening price. That is one stock with no aggregate investor-loss data, and the year is unfinished.

reviews.rationale: The named year 2026 had not ended by the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. No conclusive event shows substantial losses for both retail investors and index funds, or rules them out. The single-stock drawdown is context only.

attribution.note: Marcus's own numbered argument in his post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will wind up overpaying'. Narrowing 'everybody' to the competing AI developers matches the passage. The competitive regime is kept as a qualifier.

contract.note: Reading 'overpaying' as lifetime attributable returns that fail to cover AI investment costs is a fair, ordinary reading. It calls competition an antecedent while setting condition_status to not_applicable, a minor inconsistency that does not change the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 is a company disclosure that it faces intense competition now. It bears on the condition, not on eventual returns, so it cannot support the outcome.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and no completed investment history in the packet shows insufficient returns for every developer or a clear counterexample. Current competition is documented only by a company's own disclosure, and eventual returns are unknown.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: A causal claim: pricing restrictions will cause customer reconsideration. 'About using them' slightly narrows 'think twice', but the contract reads reconsideration broadly, so it is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading the buffet metaphor as restricting generous bundled usage, with widespread reconsideration as the effect, is ordinary and fair. Requiring representative customer evidence is reasonable.

evidence.note: May 13 company announcement of a separate credit for programmatic usage. It shows a planned change before the post but nothing about customer response.
May 6 company disclosure that some Claude Code limits were doubled. This weakens a blanket reading of the premise.
June 15 notice pausing the announced Agent SDK change. The specific restriction was not carried out, but announcements and other providers are not covered.
Consumer panel shows fewer users leaving Claude from June to September. It does not isolate affected plans or effects of pricing, so it cannot settle causation.

reviews.rationale: The premise was only partly met: a change was announced before the post, but limits were raised elsewhere and the change was paused. No representative evidence links any restriction to widespread customer reconsideration, or rules it out. Switching data do not isolate pricing effects.
